parts.text: The LORD declares his love for Israel, answering their doubts by contrasting his dealings with Jacob and Esau. Edom may try to rebuild, but God will overthrow its proud recovery. Israel will see that the LORD’s greatness extends beyond its own borders.

God then confronts priests who fail to honor him as father and master. They offer blind, lame, and sick animals they would not dare present to a governor, and treat worship as wearisome. He rejects their corrupt offerings and condemns those who promise a worthy animal but substitute a defective one. The Lord declares himself a great King whose name will be honored among the nations.

The priests are warned that failure to honor God’s name will turn their blessings into a curse. Levi’s covenant of life and peace is recalled as a model of reverence, truthful instruction, and turning people from sin. The present priests have instead corrupted the covenant, shown partiality, and caused many to stumble.

Judah’s unfaithfulness also appears in marriages connected with foreign worship and betrayal of the wife of one’s youth. Tears at the altar cannot replace fidelity to the marriage covenant. God condemns putting away and violence, urging the people to guard their spirit. They further weary him by calling evildoers good or questioning whether the God of judgment will act.

chapters.title: The coming messenger and God’s remembrance

parts.text: God will send a messenger to prepare his way, and the Lord will come to his temple. His coming is like refining fire, purifying Levi and exposing sorcery, adultery, false oaths, and oppression. Because he does not change, Jacob is not consumed. He calls the people to return, including bringing the tithes and offerings they have withheld, and promises blessing upon their land.

Some argue that serving God is useless because the proud and wicked prosper. Those who fear the LORD, however, speak together, and he hears them. A book of remembrance records those who honor his name. He promises to claim and spare them as treasured possessions, making the distinction between the righteous and wicked plainly visible.

chapters.title: The coming day and Elijah’s mission

parts.text: The coming day will burn like an oven, consuming the proud and wicked like stubble. For those who fear the LORD’s name, however, the Sun of righteousness will rise with healing. They will go forth with renewed freedom and strength, while the wicked become ashes beneath their feet.

Israel is called to remember the law given through Moses at Horeb, including its statutes and judgments. Before the great and dreadful day of the LORD, God promises to send Elijah the prophet. His work will turn the hearts of fathers and children toward one another, lest the LORD come and strike the earth with a curse.
